_comment: Narration. One voice, one TTS pass per line, placed against the timeline by scripts/build_audio.py. Placement is relative to a timeline entry so the edit can be reordered without recomputing absolute times. Run scripts/animatic.py --check-only after any change here.
_density_note: Speaking density is the dial that controls whether this feels austere or crowded. The first draft ran 440 words over 130s (140% density - unplayable). This draft is deliberately terse: every line states its impossibility once, as logistics, and stops. If a line feels like it wants another clause, it does not.

voice.description: Generic British RP, male, 50s. Measured, unhurried, faintly bored. Reading a record, not telling a story.
voice.direction: Never marvel. Never emphasise the impossible detail - deliver it at exactly the same weight as the grid reference. Fall slightly at the end of each sentence. No upward inflection, no warmth, no smile.
voice.forbidden: Do not clone or approximate David Attenborough or any other identifiable living broadcaster. A recognisable voice makes the film about the impersonation and turns an art piece into a deepfake.

lines.text: Four species that cannot be reliably observed. The following footage is the best available.
A hedgerow in Somerset. Eleven weeks of continuous filming.
Noctuella evanescens is present in this frame.
It cannot be filmed directly. The species is absent from wherever the operator is attending.
Only at the frame edge. Only out of focus.
That is the specimen.
No centred image was obtained. This is routine.
Automatic cameras, with no operator present, return empty frames.
The requirement is not the camera. It is the attention.
lines.note: Plants the word the film ends on.

lines.text: The Survey lists it as common.
Eleven minutes past four. A right whale surfaces west of the Hebrides.
Eleven minutes past four. A right whale surfaces off the Kaikoura Trench.
lines.note: Deliberately near-identical to vo11. The repetition is the evidence. shot08 carries no narration at all - the callosity pattern is held in silence.

lines.text: The callosity pattern is identical. Callosities identify an individual.
The Survey records one animal.
Neither body has been observed to travel.
Catalogued separately for nineteen years, until the night both were filmed at once.
It is not known what the animal was before that.
lines.note: The only foreshadow in the film. Establishes that observation does things, so the appendix is a rule the audience has been taught rather than a twist.

lines.text: A wax cylinder, 1890. A hedgerow outside Ludlow.
Last April. The same hedgerow.
Consecutive notes of the same song.
The song takes three to four hundred years. The Survey holds nine notes.
No individual has heard more than one note.
The species is not thought to know that it is singing.
One further species. It has not been named.
No footage exists. It has never been photographed.
It comes into existence upon being observed. One instance per observer.
At the beginning of this programme, the known population was three hundred and twelve.
lines.note: Must land clear of the chyron tick at 6.25s into shot16. The two seconds of silence between this line and the tick are load-bearing.

lines.text: The Survey thanks you for your attention.
lines.note: Last word of the film is 'attention', which vo09 established as the mechanism. That callback is what makes the taxonomy a system rather than a list.

notes.prompt: A single sustained song thrush note, one clean fluting phrase, recorded outdoors, no other birds, no music, no reverb.
notes.note: Generated clean and degraded in ffmpeg. Never ask a model for a period recording - it invents damage that will not match the modern note.

notes.prompt: A single sustained song thrush note at a different pitch, one clean fluting phrase, close modern field recording, no other birds, no music.

ambience.prompt: Continuous quiet English hedgerow ambience, late autumn, overcast: wind in dry hawthorn and bramble, occasional water dripping from leaves, a distant rook. No birdsong, no insects, no human sound, no music.
Open ocean ambience from a small vessel: swell, wind across a microphone, water against a hull. No gulls, no engine, no voices, no music.
Quiet spring hedgerow ambience at dusk, close and intimate, faint wind, no birdsong, no music.
Very quiet hedgerow at last light, wind dropping to almost nothing, no birds, no insects, no music.

archive_layer._comment: The 1890 shellac degradation. Synthesised in ffmpeg, no model required - see SHELLAC in scripts/build_audio.py. Applied to note_1890 only, and gone by the time the picture resolves into the modern plate.
archive_layer.filters: highpass=300, lowpass=3200, vibrato for wow and flutter, hard compression
archive_layer.note: The joke in Specimen 003 lives entirely in this transition: bandlimited shellac resolving into clean modern field recording sells four hundred years better than any image could.

room_tone._comment: Low-level pink noise under the entire film so that cuts to silence read as recorded quiet rather than as a dropout.
